summary: Mission Control Clicker is a browser-based incremental game that teaches how space missions are designed and why each destination is hard. You collect science data and spend it on instruments and mission upgrades. This lets you launch missions to the Moon, asteroid Bennu, Mars and Jupiter’s moon Europa. As you unlock each mission, you also unlock short, illustrated lessons about its real challenges, such as signal delay, radiation, thin atmospheres and weak sunlight.
details:
What it does

Mission Control Clicker is a browser game about space missions. You tap to collect science data, spend it on instruments like cameras, radar and rovers, and use the data to launch missions to the Moon, Bennu, Mars and Europa. As you progress, you unlock short lessons with pictures about why each place is hard to explore, such as radiation, weak sunlight and long signal delays. Random space events give bonus data.

Benefits and impact

It teaches how real space missions work through play instead of a textbook. We hope it gets students curious about space science and engineering.

Tools

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one web page, with canvas for the planet view and Web Audio for sound. We used Claude, an AI assistant, to help write the code and text. [Add what your team did, like checking facts against NASA pages.]

Creativity

It mixes a clicker game with real NASA mission facts and a shuttle-cockpit look with a gray and green analog control panel. Lessons unlock as a reward for progress.

What we considered

It runs on any device with no download or account. The facts come from real NASA missions but are simplified so the game stays fun. We kept the colors calm and added a sound button and reduced-motion support.
